messages:
maria: FYI saw a perf regression in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's continuous-batching tweak. p99 token latency up and hit-rate down. Anyone else?

sam: saw alerts. numbers?

maria: quick snapshot from prod (last 1h):
```
- prefix-cache hit-rate: 62% -> 38% (pre/post change)
- overall token cost: +12%
- p50 token latency: 12ms -> 15ms
- p95 token latency: 38ms -> 62ms
- p99 token latency: 120ms -> 210ms
- fraction of mixed batches (prefix + no-prefix): 18% -> 52%
```

cheng: ugh. that batch mixing stat jumps out — continuous batching is aggressively filling windows and mixing short-prefix requests with cold ones. when we mix, cache hits go down because keying is per-client prefix variant.

kevin: do we have keying collisions or normalizations changed? I remember a change to trim trailing whitespace from the key last week.

maria: we rolled a kernel selection + batching heuristic PR (runtime#4127). keying change was just normalization (strip EOL), not a semantic change. But the batching policy now waits up to 6ms to assemble bigger batches, and it favors filling with anything available which increases heterogeneity.

sam: quick profiler dump from a representative shard (10k reqs):
```
BATCH_SIZE_DIST: 1:24% 2:33% 4:20% 8+:23%
BATCH_COMPOSITION:
  all-prefix: 28%
  mixed-prefix: 52%
  no-prefix: 20%
CACHE_HIT_BY_BATCH_TYPE:
  all-prefix: 78%
  mixed-prefix: 32%
  no-prefix: 4%
```

eva: so mixed batches kill effective hit-rate because the batch holds diverse KV keys; our server-side KV cache lookup is per-request and eviction/parallelism causes misses. Also warmup doesn't help since warmup assumes similar front-of-batch sequences.

cheng: two quick levers: (1) prefer homogeneous batches (grouping by prefix fingerprint) at enqueue time, (2) smarter warmup prefetch for detected hot prefixes. grouping reduces batch fill rate slightly but increases hit-rate — need tradeoff numbers.

kevin: we experimented with a grouping semaphore in staging: equal throughput, hit-rate went 40% -> 67% and p95 improved ~25ms. But tail got worse for ultra-low latency banner traffic because some single-request flows waited for grouping.

maria: exactly the tradeoff — latency vs hit-rate. We should consider class-based policies: low-latency route (no grouping, immediate dispatch), throughput route (group by prefix). runtime supports per-route policy; we can default to grouping for heavy embedding/generation routes.

sam: also suspect cache key granularity. current key: sha256(prefix + model_version + quant_bits). If prompts include volatile timestamps/usernames we get poor grouping. Maybe canonicalize placeholders when available.

maria: example canonicalizer we used in a quick patch:
```
def canonicalize_prefix(p):
    p = strip_user_tokens(p)  # replace <USER_*> tokens
    p = re.sub(r"\s+"," ", p).strip()
    return p[:1024]
```

cheng: +1. Also propose a hybrid batching rule: attempt to form homogeneous groups for up to 4ms; after that, fallback to current grouping to avoid excessive queuing. That gives most of the hit-rate benefit without large tail latency regrowth.

kevin: can we run an A/B: region-A kernel+heuristic old vs region-B new? We need short-window histograms (p50,p95,p99) and effective token costs by route and by batch type.

maria: will spin up AB tomorrow. Action items:
- sam: run a replay of last 24h traffic through simulator to quantify tail vs cost (assign: sam)
- cheng: prototype grouping-with-timeout heuristic in runtime (assign: cheng)
- kevin: prepare canary config to route 10% traffic to grouping variant (assign: kevin)
- eva: add instrumentation for "batch homogeneity" tag and per-batch cache hit breakdown (assign: eva)

eva: quick note — if we prefetch for hot prefixes we need to throttle to avoid spiking GPU memory usage. prefetched KV should be LRU and size-bounded.

maria: good call. also watch for regressions in kernel selection: some kernels expect regular sequence lengths; grouping can change distribution and lead to suboptimal kernel picks. include kernel-select traces in the A/B.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary rollout: grouping-heuristic v1 -> 10% prod at 2026-03-18T02:00:00Z

sam: will post replay results here when ready. short-term rollback plan: revert batching heuristic flag and revert normalization if regression persists.

kevin: thanks everyone. next sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow 10am to review AB telemetry. :thumbsup:
